0fbc5bb898648525.why: This is the cause of regressions 1 and 2. With no trigger of its own and no use read, an option goes to When unclear even when its rule's own words give the duration it is in force for. Scope (c) puts options of listed rules under Active now 'for its duration'. 'When unclear' is only for timing that cannot be read. Might of Khorne: Blood Tithe says 'At the start of the Command phase, you can spend … to activate one of the following abilities until the end of the battle' (data.js; same on Wahapedia world-eaters). Its moment is Blood Tithe's, already To do now in both Command phases. Its duration is every phase after that. The previous To do now placement was not right either: the spending is Blood Tithe's line. Mantra of Discipline, Binharic Courage (Aura) and Shroudpsalm (Aura): Canticles of the Omnissiah says 'At the start of your Command phase, select one of the abilities in the Canticles of the Omnissiah section. Until the start of your next Command phase, this model has that ability.' (Wahapedia Belisarius Cawl errata, the same). From Command · Your turn that covers every phase of both turns, and the entry already carries it as pk. The fix uses the rule's own-words duration (oc), or pk, as the option's Active now phases, and keeps x only when no duration is read. derive.js must write oc. In ruleTables, after ckEntry for rules (line 807) and abilities (line 846), add `{ const oc = optCover(r.text, own, r.table, ce.x && r.at ? { at:r.at } : ce); if(oc) ce.oc = oc; }`, and the same with ab.text, own, null, ce. optCover(text, own, table, e) returns null unless optionsOf(rulesText(text), table) is non-empty. Otherwise it returns coverOf(the duration that comes first in plain(own)) when that has u. It would be safer to limit it to the 'until …' durations, because 'this turn' in Cabal of Sorcerers ('not yet attempted a Ritual this turn') reads as a duration; all of Cabal's options have u, so this does no harm today. Tested in a scratch copy (derive --write, build, every list rendered). Might of Khorne moves from When unclear to Active now in all 10 sections (big-demons-baby). Mantra of Discipline, Binharic Courage and Shroudpsalm move to Active now in all 10 sections (purge-goes-the-foe). Kindred Sorcery's once-per-battle boxes stay in Command · Your turn (via). No other line changes. Aegis Protocol stays When unclear, because 'it remains in that protocol until it enters a different one' is not a duration DURATIONS reads (owner). render.js's oe fallback needs the same change.

Shooting types are what a unit that is "selected to shoot" resolves. Making Attacks (04) has "the active player" resolve every shot, and in the opponent's turn only 01.03 makes the overwatching player active: "Each time a unit is selected to shoot or selected to fight, that unit’s controlling player is the active player until those attacks are resolved." 225510c7f65187ce.why: data.js carries the todo's code byte for byte. 'own' is in HIDE unless opts.keep names it. The app calls resolveArmies(ARMIES, DATASHEETS, TABLE_ORDER) with no opts, so own never reaches a unit or row, from the datasheet or from the entry. No ARMIES entry stores own (tables.js skips it on entries), and the DATASHEETS rows carry the value as the plain stat (Deathwatch Terminator Sergeant W:'3', Impulsor InSv:'–', both GW's per the cached Wahapedia pages). The own block runs only for stats rows with from, and only under keep 'own' (tables.js --expand). It records the datasheet's value of each from-field that differs from the entry's value. Because ds is the uncopied datasheet row, nothing is mutated: row is a put() of a copy. sameLists strips own, so the tables gate compares only what the app sees, and it passes (141 entries, 18 lists). The app's resolved DW Terminator rows are W 4/4/3 with from Storm Shield on the two shield bearers, as before.

(2) The attacks match: kind:'ranged' means the line only appears with the unit’s ranged weapons, and the rule covers only “ranged attacks”. (3) The condition matches: “vs targets within 9"” means attacks against a target unit within 9", which is the rule’s “that target a unit within 9"”. Nothing is added: no visibility, closest-target or once-per-phase limit. Nothing is lost. (4) The phase is right: WHEN is “Your Shooting phase, when a friendly ORKS INFANTRY unit is selected to shoot”. It is shown once on the detachment label. Ambiguity: the rule does not say what the 9" is measured from. The usual reading is the shooting unit (“your unit”). The footnote sits under this unit’s ranged weapons, so it reads the same way and is no vaguer than the rule. The old wording “target within 9"” had the same open point. The Fires of Mars lasts “until the start of your next Command phase”, so the Imperatives also work in the opponent’s turn: in their Shooting phase (Analytic Reprisals in this list: a SKITARII INFANTRY unit “can shoot as if it were your Shooting phase”), and at the end of their Movement phase (Fire Overwatch, where Conqueror’s AP +1 still applies to snap shots), as well as in either Fight phase. 3617145e79607863.why:
Two concrete defects (tested against HEAD, then with the fix in a scratch copy, where import-test.js passes: 16/16 identical, 44 negatives, 131 checks, 0 failures).
(1) A top-level selection that is no known one is silently accepted when its entry id is an Object.prototype name, because T = D.bsIds is a plain object literal and T.info[id] is then inherited. 6 bigs with sels.unshift({id:'q', name:'Knight Castellan', entryId:'aaaa::constructor', number:1, type:'upgrade'}) imports (OK knight-destrier×2, knight-errant, knight-paladin×2, knight-warden). Adding a child {name:'Knight Castellan', entryId:'zz::toString', type:'model'} under an entry 'aaaa::hasOwnProperty' imports too, because T.infoKids is inherited the same way. That breaks “every other top-level selection … with known choices only” and the owner's rule that anything else is refused. A catalogueId of 'constructor' also hits T.factions.constructor and ends in “it could not be read” instead of “faction … not recognized”. The fix makes null-prototype copies of the tables. Both inputs are then refused with “selection Knight Castellan not recognized” / “selection Extra not recognized”, and the catalogue one with “faction Imperial Knights not recognized”.
(2) “A unit taken again as its copies” fails when the same unit comes from two lists of the pool. princes with its second Daemon Prince of Khorne swapped for a third Forgefiend (1910 pts) imports as forgefiend ×2 plus a separate forgefiend-2. picks reuses princes' Forgefiend up to its copies:2, then takes standard's Forgefiend (same detachments, so it is in the pool). The two are different objects, so `made` (keyed by object) does not merge them. They are identical field for field (JSON equal apart from copies). The fix keys `made` by the unit's JSON without copies, giving forgefiend ×3. (6 bigs with a third Knight Destrier merges only because no other IK list has a Destrier.)
The rest holds. Warlord, enhancement, Epic Hero, points limit/total, battle size, dispositions, config, Show/Hide children, holders and leader-attachment checks all behave as the item says (the gate's 44 negatives plus my probes: self-association, a cycle, an association to undefined, unit ×0, a string cost, no costLimits). Noted but within the spec's own carve-out (“max per list that no modifier changes”): 6 bigs with 4 Knight Destriers imports (1800 pts). BSData's force max of 3 (constraint 4632-a555-f127-f48c) has a modifier that sets it to 2, so it is not in maxPerList.

466219869d462b9f.why: Matches the file. Both additions work on their target cases: "if that attack has the [LETHAL HITS] ability, that ability does not apply", "that enemy unit loses the Lethal Hits ability", and "Each time an attack targets this unit, add 1 to the Hit roll" are no longer bonuses. They change no current sentence (0 diffs, 0 gaps). But each one drops the unit's OWN bonus in plausible wordings, and a dropped bonus is a hole in the gate. Tested, missed today: (1) The lost-ability test runs over the whole sentence and matches any "lost … ability". So "If this model has lost one or more wounds, its melee weapons have the [LETHAL HITS] ability." gives nothing, and neither does the same sentence without the comma. "… that enemy unit cannot use the Feel No Pain ability, and this unit's weapons have [LETHAL HITS]", "… have [LETHAL HITS], and enemy units within 6\" lose the Stealth ability" and "models in that unit have the Lethal Hits ability; if this model is destroyed, that unit loses this ability" also give nothing. (2) The drawback test uses SELF, which also covers "that unit", "that model", "it" and "your unit", and it exempts only "this unit/model makes". So a friendly attack on the chosen enemy loses its +1: "each time a friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES model within 6\" makes an attack that targets that unit, add 1 to the Wound roll" and "each time a model in that unit makes an attack that targets that unit, add 1 to the Hit roll" both give nothing. It also misses the enemy's "a ranged attack targets this unit, add 1 to the Hit roll" and "an enemy unit makes a ranged attack that targets this unit", which are stricter only. The fix does three things. It tests the drawback only on attacks that target this unit / this model / the bearer (ranged or melee too), unless a non-enemy unit or model makes the attack. It reads grants clause by clause, dropping a clause that says lose / lost / cannot use … ability (within 30 characters) or "… does not apply" in that clause or the next. And it does not split at a comma inside a bracket. Tested on 23 cases (all as expected, including "[LETHAL HITS: non-MONSTER, non-VEHICLE]" and "[ASSAULT], [HEAVY] and [LETHAL HITS]"). Over the 490 current sentences it gives 0 differences from the current code and 0 gaps, and the strip test is unchanged (157 flagged).

568bc755fedfbd58.why: I ran onceTag over every ability in all 6 lists. Branch 1 copies a BSData tag that starts "Once/Twice per" and drops the " · …" suffix, e.g. Bomb Squig "Once per turn, twice per battle, per unit", Supreme Kunnin’ "Once per phase, per army", Twisted Sorceries "Once per battle · Psychic" → "Once per battle". Branch 2 copies the text’s own words: a leading "Once per turn" (Harpoon Barbs, Malign Presence) or a parenthesised "(Once per battle, per army)" (Archslaughterer, Umbralefic Crystal). It adds ", per army" only when the text says "one model from your army with this ability" (Will of the Hive Mind → "Once per battle round, per army"; BSData tags the same wording on Direct the Slaughter "Once per battle round, per army"). No limit is invented. Latent gaps, and they leave text out rather than add to it, so this stays ok: an unparenthesised "Once per battle" after a "… model only." sentence gets no tag (enhancements Incandaeum and Null Nodules, neither in any list), and a tag-less text "Once per turn, twice per battle, …" would be cut to "Once per turn". Bomb Squig has its tag, so it is not affected.

From the end of your opponent's turn, it covers your next turn. Fulgrim's Daemon Primarch of Slaanesh (at the start of the opponent's Command phase) correctly gets pk every phase, both turns (main had pk x and t command:either). Through the skip-until edit its t is now command:opp, the same as the stored label. In the rendered checklist, Daemonic Speed is Active now in both Fight phases. One edge case is wrong. A trigger at the start of the battle round is read as both players' Command phases, so oppnext (and the existing yournext) from it adds the whole of the opponent's (or your) turn. That is never right, because at the start of a round the opponent's next turn is the one in this round, and how much the effect covers depends on who goes first. The case is not used in data.js. The fix returns x (When unclear) for yournext and oppnext from the start of the battle round, as is already done for "phase". With it, data.js and derive.json are byte-identical.

8b24aca160a7f050.why: Today it classifies correctly. Of the 4 readings with weapon and set, only Possessed Lord is a one-off; Blitz Dem Gitz! (vs non-MONSTER/VEHICLE, always), Vengeance for the Omnissiah (after a VEHICLE dies, for the rest of the battle) and Battle Protocols (a protocol picked each Command phase) have no "once per battle" in their when, tag or text, so they rightly stay in the cells ("8 (+6)", "/6", "(+2)"). But the test is too wide. (1) /\bonce per battle\b/ also matches "once per battle round": \b falls between "battle" and " round". data.js has 9 tags "Once per battle round…" and 13 such phrases in texts, and the test already returns true for Necromechanic (when "once per battle round", a guard, so no effect today). A future per-round reading with weapon and set would leave the cell wrongly. (2) Matching the whole ability text catches an ability that has an always-on bonus and a separate once-per-battle sentence. Possessed Lord says it in both when and tag, so the text adds nothing that tag and when do not already cover. Every once-per-battle ability in data.js carries a "Once per battle" tag, so dropping the text test misses none of today's readings. Not covered either way: "twice per battle" (tag "Once per turn, twice per battle, per unit") is not a one-off by this rule; the owner's rule says once per battle, so that is consistent.

So the note is a checked fact.
I spot-checked every mark in data.js against its rule text, and each one grants that value to that weapon in that list:
- Relentless Rage "Friendly WORLD EATERS units’ melee attacks have +1 A": A on every hurrdurr melee weapon; all units are Faction: World Eaters.
- Berzerker Glaive "+1 A and D … melee weapons (excluding Extra Attacks weapons) equipped by the bearer": Daemon Prince strike/sweep, which have no EXTRA ATTACKS.
- Kustom Dakka "This unit’s ranged attacks have [IGNORES COVER]": Mek plus Tankbustas/Flash Gitz ranged weapons, which form one attached unit per 19.04.
- Dakka! Dakka! Dakka! "Friendly ORKS INFANTRY units’ ranged attacks have [ASSAULT]": only INFANTRY units (Big Mek, Warboss, Mek units, Gretchin). The conditional "+3\" R" is not marked.
- Supa-snazz Dakka "Snazzgun weapons have [RAPID FIRE 1]": only group Snazzgun (Cutta, Dakka, Kill Shot).
- Empyric Guidance "While this model is leading a unit, weapons equipped by models in that unit have [LETHAL HITS]": both led units, including the leader, per 19.04 "apply to every model in an attached unit".
- Icon of Flame "(excluding CHARACTERS)": Rubric Marines’ Malefic Curse and soulreaper only.
- More Dakka: IGNORES COVER only; SUSTAINED HITS 1 "if riled up" is not marked.
- Also correct: Nazdreg’s Know-wotz, Supa-glowy Fing, Brutal But Kunnin’, Cybork Boosta, Aggressive Advance (M 10" while leading), Eldritch Vortex (PSYCHIC weapons S and D), Synaptoprescience (4+ InSv), Destabilising Predation (ANTI-CHARACTER 2+).
No wrong mark found.

be8c973c18c5fe88.why:
I tested perBattle on every ability, army rule, detachment rule, enhancement and stratagem in data.js:
- Bomb Squig "Once per turn, twice per battle, per unit" → n 2, per unit.
- Makari "Once per battle, per army" and Archslaughterer, Umbralefic Crystal, Morgog’s Finkin’ Cap, Mysterious Guardian "(Once per battle, per army)" → n 1, army.
- Protean Purpose "(Once per battle, per unit)" → n 1, per unit.
- Possessed Lord, Twisted Sorceries, Resilient Organism ("this model"), Fix Dat Armour Up and Boss’ Ammo Runt ("Once per battle, per unit") → n 1, per unit.
- Every "once per battle round" text gives null: Direct the Slaughter, Will of the Hive Mind, Intimidating Motivation, Keep Huntin’ and Blessings of Khorne "activate each Blessing of Khorne once per battle round".
- Insane Bravery "cannot use this stratagem more than once per battle" → 1.
Per-turn and per-phase limits are never counted. Note for the caller: the armyWide=true argument overrides an explicit "per unit" (perBattle(Higher Imperatives, true).army is true). That is where the screenPregame problem below comes from; with the argument omitted, perBattle itself reads "per unit" correctly.

c25adae73c0bd607.why: It takes the first DURATIONS match anywhere in the rule's own words, and DURATIONS' 'turn' includes a bare 'this turn'. Cabal of Sorcerers' own words, 'select one model … that has not yet attempted a Ritual this turn', give data.js `oc:{u:'shooting:your,charge:your,fight:your'}`. That says its Rituals are in force in Charge and Fight of your turn, but the rule gives its options no duration (Destiny’s Ruin and Twist of Fate each say 'Until the end of the phase'). It does not show today, because every Cabal option has its own u. But if any option were left without a u, it would be placed by a guessed duration, against 'never guessed'. The third review already said to limit this to 'until …' durations. The fix counts only matches that begin with 'until'. Tested in a scratch copy with derive --write: only Cabal's oc disappears. Harbingers, Blood Tithe, Kindred Sorcery, Malefic Surge, Doctrina Imperatives, Blessings of Khorne, Canticles and Battle Protocols keep theirs. Every list's checklist is unchanged, and render.js passes.

Otherwise abilityTicks gives one set per copy (copyKey adds .i only when copies > 1). This matches the stated behaviour. Data check: Fix Dat Armour Up and Boss' Ammo Runt 'Once per battle, per unit' give 1 box each. Bomb Squig 'Once per turn, twice per battle, per unit' on Mek+Tankbustas (copies 2) gives 2 boxes × Unit 1/Unit 2. Intimidating Motivation 'Once per battle round, per army' gets no boxes, which is right. The keys match the ones screenPregame's abTicks uses, so a box ticked on the datasheet shows ticked on Pre-game. Abilities with naReason get no boxes. Readings are composed in the documented order: army rules on the unit's Rules line (case- and apostrophe-insensitive), each datasheet part, the first matching enhancement or upgrade across the list's detachments, the detachment rule and moreRules whose needs (all/any/none/rule) the resolved unit meets, then the entry's own. An entry list with names replaces the whole list in its order; null gives none. readOf, readBy and listWhy are stripped from every reading; READ keys are kept off the datasheet copy and the entry rest. Every one of the 155 datasheet readings reaches at least one unit (trace). The resolved lists equal main's except the 7 new readings. Every other table is equal once reading keys are stripped. Minor, non-blocking: (a) enhancements are matched by strict ===, not nm(), so an apostrophe variant would silently drop an enhancement's readings (none today); (b) a misspelt name in an entry's list resolves to nothing in resolveArmies, but verify/tables.js throws on it (tested); (c) helpers.js CODE_RULES.resolveArmies says 'fingerprints (readOf too) and readBy hidden' and does not name listWhy, which is also hidden.
